jobs.description:
About the Company

Our client is a successful international distributor of specialty chemicals, with operations across a number of international markets and a presence in more than 20 countries.

The group holds a strong international position and is currently working to strengthen its presence and drive further growth in the Nordics and Baltics.

You will become a pivotal part of an international organization, with excellent opportunities to influence development and shape the direction of future commercial growth.

About the Position

As Regional Director – Nordics & Baltics, you will have overall responsibility for the business unit's development, performance, and future direction in the region.

Your primary task will be to set the strategic direction and ensure the continuous development of the business. You will play a central role in translating the group's ambitions into concrete goals and results, as well as creating the organizational and commercial framework for future growth.

In close collaboration with the Sales Director, you will develop and implement the strategy for the region and ensure progress through clear leadership, prioritization, and strong cooperation with the rest of the organization.

You will establish direction and engagement within the organization, develop leaders and employees, and ensure that the right competencies and resources are brought into play. The role requires the ability to deliver results through others while maintaining a strategic overview and an understanding of the business's commercial opportunities.

Your Primary Responsibilities

• Develop leaders and employees with a focus on competencies, engagement, accountability, and collaboration.

• Translate the group's overall ambitions into concrete strategies, goals, and action plans.

• Support a company culture characterized by initiative, ownership, openness, and continuous development.

About You

You have leadership experience and a strong strategic understanding. You possess the ability to gain commitment, set direction, and develop an organization through clear leadership, involvement, and trust.

You do not necessarily need to have held a director-level position previously. The most important thing is that you have the ambition, the strategic overview, and the ability to take overall responsibility for a business unit's development and results.

We imagine that you:

• Have experience in commercial leadership and organizational development, including developing and implementing strategies and translating them into concrete goals and results.

• Are a clear leader who sets direction, builds engagement, and ensures progress.

• Thrive with overall responsibility and are able to maintain both the strategic overview and an understanding of the organization's daily operations.

• Are a modern leader who believes in freedom with responsibility and is motivated by coaching and facilitating rather than micromanaging.

• Have experience in developing people and achieving results through others.

• Possess a good financial understanding and the ability to make decisions on a sound strategic and financial basis.

• Have experience from the specialty chemicals industry or related sectors. This will be considered an advantage.

• Communicate effortlessly in both Danish and English. Additional language skills are an advantage.

What Is Offered

• A central leadership position with responsibility for an international business unit that is part of a successful global group.

• A commercial mandate with the opportunity to influence strategy and organization and leave a clear mark on the development of the Nordics and Baltics.

• A dynamic working environment combining strategic responsibility, leadership, and organizational development.

• Business travel in connection with the development of the business in the Nordics and Baltics, with significant influence over your own travel planning.

Workplace: Aarhus area.

You can be based anywhere in Denmark, as there are good opportunities for remote work. If you live outside daily commuting distance, you will be expected to work from the office approximately once a week.

At Struers, we help companies and laboratories around the world understand their materials and make confident decisions about quality. Our purpose is Ensuring Certainty, and behind the equipment that delivers that certainty is increasingly sophisticated software.

We are looking for a Software Engineer to help develop the machine-control software behind our next generation of products.

Our machine-control platform is based on modern PLC technology, but this is not a traditional PLC programming role. We approach machine control as a software engineering discipline, applying principles such as structured architecture, modularity, reuse, design patterns, automated testing, and maintainable code.

Whether your background is embedded software, automation, control engineering, C/C++, C#, or PLC development, we are interested in strong software engineers who enjoy making software interact with the physical world.

You will contribute from early concepts through product launch, developing reusable software components, machine behavior, and control algorithms, and validating your solutions directly on real machines.

Key Responsibilities:

• Implement machine control and process logic for Struers machines.

• Design control algorithms and implement software designs based on input from software architects.

• Develop and improve reusable software modules and libraries for Struers machines.

• Apply modern software engineering principles to create robust, modular, testable, and maintainable machine software.

• Test and verify software directly on real machines and equipment.

• Work closely with mechanical, hardware, and project teams.

• Participate in R&D product projects from concept phase to product launch.

• Contribute to code reviews and analysis of other developers’ work.

• Establish required design, test, and product documentation.

• Support handover of product software and documentation to the engineering department responsible for product and platform maintenance.

• Collaborate with international software colleagues, including the Czech software team.

• Demonstrate the ability and willingness to use AI tools to improve productivity, decision-making, work quality, and cost efficiency.

• Identify appropriate AI use cases and critically evaluate AI-generated outputs.

Requirements:

Education & Experience:

Must-have:

• Relevant engineering degree or similar technical background.

• Hands-on software development experience.

• Ability to develop structured and maintainable software.

• Experience from at least one relevant software development technology, for example, C/C++, C#, Java, PLC programming, or another structured or object-oriented programming language.

• Interest in automation, machine control, PLC-based systems, embedded software, or industrial software development.

• Ability and motivation to work with physical equipment and test software on real machines.

• Good communication skills in English, both spoken and written.

Nice-to-have:

• Experience with machine control, process logic, automation systems, or control/regulation.

• Experience with object-oriented programming.

• Experience with Structured Text or PLC programming.

• Experience designing or implementing control algorithms.

• Experience from industrial equipment, machinery, production equipment, or similar domains.

• Experience working in international engineering teams.

Professional skills:

• Structured and analytical approach to software development.

• Ability to understand software designs and implement them in a maintainable way.

• Ability to work close to physical products and solve practical engineering problems.

• Strong collaboration skills across software, hardware, mechanical, and project disciplines.

• Ability to take responsibility for implementation tasks within product projects.

• Interest in building robust, reusable, and maintainable software solutions.

• Good communication skills and ability to contribute positively in an international team.

• Self-motivated and focused on moving tasks toward completion.

• Curious and willing to learn Struers’ products, domain, platform, and development practices.

Success Criteria:

• High-quality machine-control software is delivered according to project needs and the agreed software architecture.

• Machine control and process logic are implemented in a structured, maintainable, and reusable way.

• Software is tested and verified systematically on real machines and equipment.

• Reusable software modules and libraries contribute to reduced development time across projects.

• Software design and implementation meet relevant quality, maintainability, cost, and compliance expectations.

• The role contributes positively to collaboration between software, mechanical, hardware, and project teams.

• The role contributes to effective collaboration across locations, including with the Czech software team.

• Product software and documentation are handed over in a structured way to the engineering department responsible for product and platform maintenance.

About the Business Unit

Struers is an AMETEK business unit and a global leader in materialographic and metallographic solutions, providing equipment, consumables, software, and services for material testing, sample preparation, and hardness testing. Its technologies help manufacturers, research institutions, and laboratories analyze materials and ensure the highest standards of quality, reliability, and performance across industries such as aerospace, automotive, electronics, energy, and advanced manufacturing.

Founded in 1875 in Denmark and headquartered in Ballerup, Denmark, Struers has more than 150 years of expertise in material science and a global presence with offices and support teams worldwide. Known for its strong application knowledge, innovation, and customer-focused approach, Struers helps organizations achieve accurate and reproducible material analysis results that support product development, quality control, and scientific advancement.

For more information, visit www.ametek.com/ and www.struers.com/en

About Be My Eyes

Be My Eyes is on a mission to make the world more accessible for the 340 million people who are blind or have low vision. Our apps connect people with volunteers, companies and AI through live video, free of charge, so they can handle the inaccessible parts of everyday life at home and at work.

The idea came from Hans Jørgen Wiberg, a Danish craftsman with low vision. The app launched in 2015, drew 10,000 volunteer sign-ups in its first 24 hours, and now has millions of volunteers helping in more than 180 languages. Today our products include the Be My Eyes app, Be My AI, Be My Eyes for Smart Glasses, the Service Directory and Be My Eyes for Desktop.

We build products with our community, not just for it, and their needs come first even when that challenges our own assumptions. We move fast, care about the details and take ownership of what we ship. We see mistakes as part of pushing boundaries, and we take kindness seriously while keeping room for fun.

Read more about our story

About the role

You'll own the "how" of product development. The role sits where engineering leadership meets hands-on technical work: you'll lead engineers across mobile, web and backend, and stay close enough to the code to make real technical calls.

You'll partner closely with Product and Design to ship software that blind and low vision users depend on daily. You'll also grow the people on your team, so they leave each year stronger engineers than they started it.

Small team, global impact

Few places let you work on a small team and still reach millions of people. Our whole product and engineering team is about 12 people. What we ship directly shapes the quality of life of blind and low vision people around the world.

We're also working to reach the rest of the 340 million people who are blind or have low vision, wherever they live and whatever device they use. Our tools are free for the people who rely on them. We build them to improve lives, not to make a quick profit.

For your career, that means rare scope. Your decisions reach real people fast, and you'll see the difference your team makes.

4+ years in software engineering and engineering leadership

Strong enough technically to read code, make architectural calls and unblock engineers

A track record of developing engineers — coaching them and growing their careers, not just managing their work

• 
Comfort with ambiguity and competing priorities

• 
Real care about accessibility and about building with the people who use what you ship

Nice to have

• 
Lived experience as a blind or low vision person

• 
Experience shipping iOS or Android apps that work well with VoiceOver or TalkBack

• 
Experience building or running AI- or LLM-powered product features

• 
Hands-on time with Python/Django, React or Kubernetes

•

Open to everyone

We welcome applicants of every age, gender and ability. If you don't tick every box above but the role excites you, we'd still like to hear from you.

jobs.occupation: Part-time Lecturers in International Business or Business & Government | CBS - Copenhagen Business School
jobs.description:
A number of positions as Part-time Lecturers in International Business and Business & Government respectively are available at the Department of International Economics, Government and Business (EGB) for appointment as soon as possible.

EGB is a multidisciplinary department, which conducts high-quality research in the fields of international business and political science with direct relevance to business, decision-makers and the broader public.

The department delivers research-based teaching into undergraduate and graduate teaching in programs such as International Business, International Business and Politics, and International Business in Asia. To learn more about the research and teaching activities of the department, please visit the departmental website here

As part-time lecturer you will have the opportunity to apply your knowledge to educate young people and to provide them with insight into your practical experience. At CBS part-time lecturers represent an important supplement to the teaching done by researchers. Your role as part-time lecturer will also provide you with opportunities to update your theoretical knowledge, to share in discussions with ambitious students and to be part of an international academic environment.

The position is on a temporary (3 years) part-time basis, which can be extended within the framework of the Danish Fixed-Term Employment Act (Lov om tidsbegrænset ansættelse).

The position may include

• Planning and conducting teaching in Business & Government

• Planning and conducting teaching in Strategies of Multinational Corporations and Risk management

• Planning and conducting teaching in Policy-making

• Planning and conducting teaching in Political Science with an emphasis on Comparative Politics

• Online teaching—blended learning

• Student supervision

• Preparing teaching materials and exam questions

• Conducting exams and other evaluations

Qualifications

To fill this position, you are required to have a master’s degree and must have:

• High-level practical experience, which has not been gained through academic employment with a university, or

• Employment in an academic principal position with another university (e.g. as assistant professor/researcher, associate professor/senior researcher, or professor/professor with special responsibilities).

• A part-time lecturer who is employed on the merits of his or her relevant practical experience must possess in-depth, up-to-date knowledge of the possible applications of the subject/academic discipline. This knowledge is/has been acquired through employment within the subject/academic discipline.

Other skills

• In addition to having a relevant master’s degree, emphasis is placed on your specialization and professional skills within the content of the respective courses covered by the department

• You possess good collaboration skills and the ability to contribute to a good working environment

• Proficiency in both Danish and English as teaching is conducted in both Danish and English

• It is an advantage to hold a PhD in a relevant discipline

The conditions of employment and the qualification requirements are described further in the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities.

Terms of employment

Salary and employment will be in accordance with the Cirkulære om aftale om Eksterne lektorer ved universiteter m.fl. under Uddannelses- og Forskningsministeriet. The maximum number of working hours per academic year is 500 and may vary as needed in individual semesters. Remuneration is based on the number of hours, which is determined twice a year.

When employed as a part-time lecturer you must take an introductory course on university teaching organised by CBS.

You will be assigned a researcher at the department as your professional contact person. You are expected to participate in professional events relevant to your teaching and you will also be part of the department’s network of part-time lecturers.

The recruitment process

Copenhagen Business School invites all qualified candidates to apply for the position. An appointment committee will review the applications and invite a selection of qualified candidates to an interview.

• The development of next-generation MLIPs and Hessian Interatomic Potentials (HIPs) for prediction of electrochemical reactions mechanisms and rates at solid-liquid and solid-polymer interfaces in batteries and catalysts, e.g., for in-loop deployment in agentic workflows bridging experimental and simulation-based modalities.

• The development experimental of SDL modules for synthesis and testing of sustainable battery and catalyst materials and interfaces, e.g., PFAS-free binders and electrolytes, and their implementation in agentic workflows for federated deployment of experiments and simulations.

DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. The Pioneer Center CAPeX is a 13-year and 300 MDKK “Pioneer Center for Accelerating P2X Materials Discovery”, funded by the Danish Ministry of Higher Education and Science, the Danish National Research Foundation, the Carlsberg Foundation, the Lundbeck Foundation, the Novo Nordisk Foundation, and the Villum Foundation. CAPeX is hosted by the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) and co-hosted by Aalborg University (AAU) and unites leading experts from DTU, AAU, University of Copenhagen, Aarhus University, and the University of Southern Denmark with international partners from Stanford University, Utrecht University, Imperial College London, and the University of Toronto to form a truly Pioneering Center on P2X. Furthermore, our approach is fully aligned with relevant innovation strategies, policies, and programmes across Europe, ensuring coherence, scalability, and long-term impact._

jobs.description:
About Hemab

Hemab is building preventative treatments for serious, underserved bleeding disorders. These are therapies designed to work with the body's own biology and stop bleeds before they start, instead of treating them after they happen. We're patient-first, science-led and clinical-stage - with a pipeline that takes different scientific approaches to different patient needs.

We went public via our 2026 IPO, and we're scaling across two homes: Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark.

The role

Getting a promising treatment into a clinical trial takes more than good science. Patients need medicines and delivery devices they can rely on, made to the right standards and available when needed.

As Associate Director, QA Drug Product & Device, you'll own quality oversight of our drug product manufacturing partners and combination product development. You'll work closely with CMC, Manufacturing and device development colleagues to resolve quality risks, keep clinical supplies moving and build the quality framework Hemab needs as its pipeline advances.

What you'll do

• Ensure QA oversight of selected drug product CDMOs and fill-finish activities in collaboration with the CMC and Manufacturing team

• Ensure QA oversight of design controls and risk management for combination products, including review and approval of design control deliverables, in line with 21 CFR Part 4 and EU MDR Article 117

• QA review and approval of master and executed batch records, specifications, protocols and reports

• Oversee and manage drug product deviations, CAPAs and change controls

• Ensure batch documentation is complete and release-ready, and support the Qualified Person in the certification and release of drug product and combination product batches

• Create and review quality agreements with drug product CDMOs and suppliers

• Advise and support the CMC and Manufacturing team as quality lead for selected programs

• Participate in building and improving fit-for-purpose quality systems and processes as Hemab grows, and contribute to projects across Quality and the wider organization

What you'll bring to Hemab

• Hands-on QA experience with combination products or drug-device products, including design controls and ISO 14971 risk management

• Experience overseeing drug product CDMOs, ideally aseptic fill-finish, including audits and quality agreements

• Working knowledge of EU GMP (including Annex 1), 21 CFR Parts 210/211 and 600-610, and 21 CFR Part 4 and ISO 13485.

• A collaborative, cross-functional working style, partnering closely with CMC & Manufacturing, device development, supply chain and regulatory colleagues

• Good communication skills. English is our company language, so you are comfortable writing and speaking it professionally

• A solution-oriented and hands-on way of working, comfortable taking ownership and shaping processes as the organization evolves.

Nice to have Eligibility, or a realistic path, to act as an EU Qualified Person

• Experience with prefilled syringes, autoinjectors or other injectable delivery systems

• Danish language skills

What to expect, honestly

You'll be accountable for quality, but much of the manufacturing happens outside Hemab. That means working through CDMOs, sometimes with incomplete information, competing timelines and decisions that cannot wait. You'll need to know when to challenge, when to escalate and when there's enough evidence to move forward.

Drug product manufacturing and device development don't always move at the same pace. A late deviation, an unresolved design control issue or missing batch documentation can affect clinical supply. You'll need to get close to the detail, work directly with partners and find a compliant way forward.

Some of our quality frameworks are still being built. You'll help establish them while managing today's work. If you prefer established systems and clearly separated responsibilities, this may be frustrating. If you enjoy building sensible ways of working that protect patients without slowing good decisions, there's room to make a real difference.

Why Hemab

At Hemab, your work ultimately connects back to something simple. People living with serious bleeding disorders get something they've never had before - the chance to prevent a bleed, instead of reacting to one after it happens. You'll be joining at a stage where individual decisions still carry real weight, and where your work can help turn promising science into a preventative treatment that actually reaches patients.

How we treat our people is meant to be an extension of how we think about patients: with care, honesty, and respect. We're still building the consistency to back that up across every hiring process, every time. We'd say that plainly instead of pretending otherwise. If any part of your experience with us falls short of it, tell us.

Hemab builds balanced candidate slates and assesses everyone against a single standard. If you need a reasonable adjustment at any stage of the hiring process, please tell us.

**We are looking for a student with a strong analytical mindset and a genuine interest in optimisation, modelling and supply chain analysis. You enjoy solving complex problems with a systems approach, and you want to see your solutions work in an industrial manufacturing supply chain.

**Essential

**

• You are enrolled in an MSc programme at a Danish university within Industrial Engineering and Management, Business Analytics, Mathematical Modelling, Chemical Engineering or a related discipline.

• You have at least three semesters remaining in your studies.

• Your studies focus on supply chain, operations research and/or operations management, mathematical modelling or optimisation.

**Useful, But Not Essential

**

• A solid understanding of mathematical programming, for example from tools or languages such as Pyomo, Gurobi, Python or similar.

**What You’ll Do

**You will be part of the work that turns mathematical models into practical support for manufacturing decisions. Your tasks will vary, and will focus on mathematical programming for supply chain analysis, capacity planning, and production planning and scheduling.

• Develop and apply mathematical models, including mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) and related optimisation methods.

• Support and drive optimisation projects focused on data analysis, capacity planning, production planning and scheduling.

• Contribute to digital development and other advanced modelling initiatives within manufacturing operations.

• Bring theoretical concepts and analytical methods from your studies into real industrial challenges.

• Use data, modelling and optimisation to help colleagues make better decisions.

**You will be part of Global Manufacturing & Supply, where colleagues work across the value chain to scale processes and products for the people who need them. The group has 7 highly skilled colleagues, alongside a number of students and interns. The team has a trusting, inclusive and enthusiastic work environment. Colleagues support each other, and they look forward to making you feel welcome.

**What You Can Expect Here

**As a student, you will have the opportunity to grow by applying your academic knowledge to real-world industrial challenges. You will gain experience of working in a global company and a manufacturing environment, and learn how data, modelling and optimisation support better decision-making. You will be supported to perform at your best, trusted to take ownership and encouraged to make your voice heard.

This position is hourly paid. For this position, the hourly base rate is 241,34 DKK, based on an assessment of relevant factors such as experience, educational background, demonstrated competencies, and the specific skills required for the position.

In addition to the hourly base rate, Student Assistants are entitled to a pension scheme (currently 10% employer contribution and 5% employee contribution).

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

**Start now

**Your impact begins today. If you are ready to turn your studies into practical optimisation work in pharmaceutical manufacturing, apply for the Optimization Engineer Student role by 27 November 2026. Interviews will take place on 5 and 6 January 2027.

jobs.description:
We are looking for a Senior Patent Attorney to play a central role in protecting and enabling innovation across Demant's global business and help shape the future of our Intellectual Property function.

In this role, you will partner closely with R&D teams, engineers, scientists, and business stakeholders to ensure that Demant continues to develop and launch innovative products with the lowest possible litigation risk. You will contribute to the growth and strengthening of our international patent portfolio while providing strategic IP guidance that supports our business ambitions.

This role requires more than technical expertise and patent law knowledge. It requires curiosity, commercial understanding, good stakeholder management, and the ability to translate complex technologies into valuable intellectual property. This is where you come in.

Welcome to Demant Intellectual Property

You will join Demant's Intellectual Property team at our Demant headquarters in Smørum, just outside Copenhagen, and become part of a highly skilled and collaborative team consisting of Patent Attorneys, Trademark Attorneys, and IP Paralegals.

Demant is a growing, world-leading hearing healthcare corporation that offers solutions in hearing devices, diagnostic instruments, and intelligent audio and video equipment. Through innovative technologies and deep expertise, we are dedicated to making life-changing differences for people with hearing loss around the world.

Our team consists of 14 colleagues from several different nationalities and professional backgrounds. We believe that results are achieved through collaboration and knowledge-sharing. We actively support one another, provide constructive feedback, and continuously develop our collective expertise in both technology and intellectual property.

Working closely with globally distributed business units and R&D organizations, our primary purpose is to help ensure that Demant's products can successfully reach the market while minimizing intellectual property risks.

Help protect the innovations of tomorrow

Joining us, you will bring an intellectual property perspective to strategic technology decisions and help researchers, engineers, and business leaders navigate an increasingly complex innovation landscape.

A key part of your role will be identifying opportunities and risks early in the development process and helping stakeholders answer critical questions: Are we free to commercialize this technology? How can we strengthen our competitive position? How can we protect our innovations globally? And how do we build an IP portfolio that supports Demant's long-term business strategy?

You will work across the boundaries of technology, law, and business, helping transform ideas into protected innovations while supporting product and technology development from concept to market launch.

In this role, you will

• Support innovation throughout the product lifecycle – Participate in R&D project groups and provide IP guidance throughout the development process and help teams make informed technology and business decisions.

• Drive freedom-to-operate activities – Conduct analyses and provide strategic advice to ensure products can be launched with the lowest possible litigation risk.

• Expand and strengthen Demant's patent portfolio – Evaluate invention disclosures, identify patentable innovations, and actively contribute to the growth of our international patent portfolio.

• Manage patent drafting and prosecution – Prepare, file, and prosecute patent applications in multiple jurisdictions while working closely with inventors and external partners.

• Analyze competitor patents – Prepare, file, and present at opposition proceedings before the European Patent Office

• Develop intellectual property expertise – Contribute to the team's collective knowledge within technology and patent law while continuously expanding your own professional capabilities.

By joining Demant, you will step into a highly visible role where your ability to connect technology, intellectual property, and business strategy will directly support innovation and help protect products that improve the lives of people across the world.

What You Bring

You have a scientific or technical background combined with practical intellectual property experience and a genuine interest in understanding how innovation creates business value.

You bring:

• Qualification as a European Patent Attorney or as a US Patent Attorney.

• 5+ years of experience within intellectual property, gained either in industry, private practice, or a combination of both.

• A scientific or technical degree, preferably within physics, electronics, or a related field.

• Excellent analytical capabilities and the ability to quickly understand new technologies and technical concepts.

• Strong communication skills and the ability to explain complex IP matters clearly to a broad range of stakeholders.

• A structured and systematic approach combined with strong attention to detail.

• An interest in understanding business needs and translating them into effective IP strategies.

Finally, you are curious, collaborative, and enjoy working closely with experts across different disciplines. You combine technical depth with commercial awareness, build trusted relationships with stakeholders, and are motivated by helping innovation succeed.

Flexible Working Conditions

At Demant, we work in a collaborative environment built on trust, openness, and strong professional relationships. Networking and knowledge-sharing are essential parts of how we work.

We offer you flexible working conditions, excellent opportunities for professional development, and a highly skilled team that works towards a common goal. From the moment you enter our premises, you will experience Demant's energizing and welcoming spirit.

Join our diverse organization and work alongside colleagues from many different nationalities and backgrounds while contributing to technologies that make a meaningful difference in people's lives.

Come and join us

Please submit your application as soon as possible and no later than December 13, 2026.

Please note that we only accept applications submitted through our online recruitment system.

If you would like to know more about the position, you are welcome to contact Director of Patents & Designs, Daniel Fischer, via email at dajf@demant.com.

We are curious to meet you.

Recruitment Process Information

If you think role is exiting, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible, since we will be inviting candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis.
